papers.name: Components 1 and 2 (all content; Component 1 non-calculator, Component 2 calculator)

topics.name: Number
points: FN1 Order positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions; use the symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥
FN2 Apply the four operations, including formal written methods, to integers, decimals, simple fractions and mixed numbers; place value
FN3 Inverse operations and priority of operations, including brackets, powers, roots and reciprocals
FN4 Prime numbers, factors, multiples, HCF, LCM and prime factorisation
FN5 Systematic listing strategies
FN6 Positive integer powers and real roots; recognise powers of 2, 3, 4, 5
FN7 Calculate with roots and with integer indices
FN8 Calculate exactly with fractions and multiples of π
FN9 Calculate with and interpret standard form A × 10ⁿ
FN10 Convert between terminating decimals and their corresponding fractions
FN11 Identify and work with fractions in ratio problems
FN12 Interpret fractions and percentages as operators
FN13 Standard units of mass, length, time, money and compound measures, using decimal quantities
FN14 Estimate answers and check calculations using approximation and estimation
FN15 Round to an appropriate degree of accuracy; use inequality notation for error intervals
FN16 Apply and interpret limits of accuracy

topics.name: Algebra
points: FA1 Use and interpret algebraic notation and conventions, including fractions and brackets
FA2 Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions, including scientific formulae
FA3 Vocabulary of expressions, equations, formulae, identities, inequalities, terms and factors
FA4 Simplify and manipulate expressions: collecting like terms, expanding brackets, factorising, laws of indices
FA5 Use standard formulae and rearrange formulae to change the subject
FA6 Distinguish between equations and identities; argue that expressions are equivalent
FA7 Interpret simple expressions as functions with inputs and outputs
FA8 Work with coordinates in all four quadrants
FA9 Plot straight-line graphs; identify parallel lines; find the equation of a line through two points or one point with a gradient
FA10 Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions graphically and algebraically
FA11 Roots, intercepts and turning points of quadratic functions graphically; deduce roots algebraically
FA12 Recognise, sketch and interpret linear, quadratic, simple cubic and reciprocal graphs
FA13 Plot and interpret graphs of real situations, including simple kinematic problems
FA14 Solve linear equations in one unknown algebraically; approximate solutions from graphs
FA15 Solve quadratic equations x² + bx + c = 0 by factorising; approximate solutions from graphs
FA16 Solve two simultaneous linear equations algebraically; approximate solutions from graphs
FA17 Translate situations into equations, solve them and interpret the solution
FA18 Solve linear inequalities in one variable; represent the solution on a number line
FA19 Generate terms of a sequence from term-to-term or position-to-term rules
FA20 Recognise triangular, square, cube, arithmetic, Fibonacci-type, simple quadratic and geometric sequences
FA21 Deduce expressions for the nth term of linear sequences

topics.name: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
points: FR1 Change between related standard units and compound units
FR2 Density and pressure and their relationships with mass, volume, force and area
FR3 Use scale factors, scale diagrams and maps
FR4 Express one quantity as a fraction of another
FR5 Use ratio notation, including reduction to simplest form
FR6 Divide a quantity into parts in a given ratio; apply ratio to real contexts
FR7 Express a multiplicative relationship between two quantities as a ratio or a fraction
FR8 Understand and use proportion as equality of ratios
FR9 Relate ratios to fractions and to linear functions
FR10 Percentages: percentage change, original value, simple interest, percentages over 100%
FR11 Solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion, including graphical and algebraic representations
FR12 Use compound units such as speed, rates of pay, unit pricing, density and pressure
FR13 Compare lengths, areas and volumes using ratio notation; scale factors and similarity
FR14 Understand that X is inversely proportional to Y; interpret equations describing proportion
FR15 Interpret the gradient of a straight line graph as a rate of change; direct and inverse proportion graphs
FR16 Growth and decay problems, including compound interest

topics.name: Geometry and measures
points: FG1 Conventional terms and notation; labelling triangles; drawing diagrams from written descriptions
FG2 Ruler and compass constructions and loci; perpendicular distance as shortest distance
FG3 Angle facts at a point, on a line, vertically opposite, parallel lines; angle sums of triangles and polygons
FG4 Properties and definitions of special triangles, quadrilaterals and other plane figures
FG5 Congruence criteria SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS
FG6 Derive results about angles and sides using Pythagoras and isosceles triangles; simple proofs
FG7 Congruent and similar shapes using rotations, reflections, translations and enlargements (including fractional scale factors)
FG8 Circle definitions and properties: centre, radius, chord, diameter, circumference, tangent, arc, sector, segment
FG9 Solve geometrical problems on coordinate axes
FG10 Faces, surfaces, edges and vertices of cubes, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres
FG11 Construct and interpret plans and elevations of 3D shapes
FG12 Standard units of measure and related concepts (length, area, volume, angle, mass, time, money)
FG13 Measure lines and angles; maps, scale drawings and bearings
FG14 Area of triangles, parallelograms and trapezia; volume of cuboids and right prisms
FG15 Circumference and area of circles; surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids
FG16 Arc lengths, angles and areas of sectors
FG17 Similarity: relationships between lengths in similar figures
FG18 Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometric ratios in right-angled triangles
FG19 Exact values of sin, cos and tan for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°
FG20 Describe translations as 2D vectors
FG21 Add and subtract vectors, multiply by a scalar; diagrammatic and column representations

topics.name: Probability
points: FP1 Record, describe and analyse frequencies of outcomes using tables and frequency trees
FP2 Apply ideas of randomness, fairness and equally likely events to predict outcomes
FP3 Relate relative expected frequencies to theoretical probability on the 0–1 scale
FP4 Probabilities of an exhaustive set of outcomes sum to one
FP5 Empirical unbiased samples tend towards theoretical probability with increasing sample size
FP6 Enumerate sets systematically using tables, grids, Venn diagrams and tree diagrams
FP7 Construct theoretical possibility spaces to calculate probabilities
FP8 Probability of independent and dependent combined events using tree diagrams

topics.name: Statistics
points: FS1 Infer properties of populations from samples; limitations of sampling
FS2 Design and criticise questions for a questionnaire, including fairness
FS3 Construct and interpret tables, charts and diagrams for categorical, discrete and time series data
FS4 Compare distributions using graphs, averages (median, mean, mode), range and outliers
FS5 Apply statistics to describe a population
FS6 Scatter graphs: correlation, lines of best fit, predictions and dangers of extrapolation
